topics.title: Atmospheric Pressure and its Distribution
topics.ncert_sections: Atmospheric Pressure; Vertical Variation of Pressure; Horizontal Distribution of Pressure; World Distribution of Sea Level Pressure

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how atmospheric pressure is measured and how it decreases with height.
Describe isobars and the world pattern of sea level pressure belts and their seasonal shift.

topics.title: Forces Affecting the Velocity and Direction of Wind
topics.ncert_sections: Forces Affecting the Velocity and Direction of Wind; Pressure Gradient Force; Frictional Force; Coriolis Force

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the pressure gradient force and friction influence wind speed.
Explain how the Coriolis force deflects winds and why it varies with latitude.
Describe the geostrophic wind as a balance of pressure gradient and Coriolis forces.
Distinguish cyclonic and anticyclonic circulation and the associated convergence and divergence.

topics.title: General Circulation of the Atmosphere
topics.ncert_sections: General circulation of the atmosphere; General Atmospheric Circulation and its Effects on Oceans

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Hadley, Ferrel and polar cells and the planetary winds they produce.
Explain El Nino, the southern oscillation and the global effects of ENSO.

topics.title: Seasonal and Local Winds
topics.ncert_sections: Seasonal Wind; Local Winds; Land and Sea Breezes; Mountain and Valley Winds

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the daily reversal of land and sea breezes from differential heating.
Explain valley breezes, mountain winds, katabatic winds and warm leeward winds.
Define an air mass and classify air masses by their source regions.
Identify the types of fronts and the weather they bring.
Describe the development and occlusion of an extra tropical cyclone along the polar front.
Compare extra tropical cyclones with tropical cyclones.
State the conditions for the formation of tropical cyclones and the source of their energy.
Describe the eye, eye wall and landfall of a mature tropical cyclone.
Explain how thunderstorms and tornadoes form.
